headline: Mix shift lifts margins and profit despite a sales dip
summary_short: Qorvo's fiscal Q1 2027 (three months ended June 27, 2026) revenue fell 4.2% y/y to $784.8 million as an ACG pullback from mass-market Android phones outweighed HPA growth, but gross margin jumped to 51.1% from 40.5% and operating income more than tripled to $96.8 million, lifting diluted EPS to $0.96 from $0.27.
summary_long: Revenue fell on a strategic ACG retreat from mass-market Android smartphones (-16.6% y/y) and softer CSG Wi-Fi demand (-7.5%), partly offset by HPA's 50.2% jump on defense/aerospace and DOCSIS 4.0 demand. Gross margin expanded 10.6ppt y/y to 51.1% on that mix shift, while lower CSG-consolidation headcount costs cut opex, driving operating income to $96.8 million from $30.1 million. Net income reached $85.8 million ($0.96 diluted EPS) despite $14.9 million of Skyworks merger costs and $11.7 million of restructuring charges. Given the pending Skyworks merger, Qorvo has stopped holding earnings calls and issuing formal guidance; it now expects FY2027 non-GAAP EPS above $7.00 and still expects non-GAAP gross margin above 50%. Cash rose to $1,328.9 million; no buybacks this quarter.

drivers.explanation: ACG revenue fell $94.7M (-16.6%) on the strategic pivot away from mass-market Android smartphones; CSG fell $8.3M on softer Wi-Fi demand; HPA rose $69.0M (+50.2%) on defense/aerospace and DOCSIS 4.0 demand, only partly offsetting the declines.
Driven by the mix shift away from lower-margin, mass-market Android smartphones within ACG, plus ongoing business-mix optimization across the ACG and HPA segments.

Same ACG/HPA mix-shift strategy behind the gross-profit gain; non-GAAP gross margin (excludes stock comp, intangible amortization, restructuring charges) rose to 52.8% from 44.0%, up 880bp per the CFO.

Higher gross margin plus lower R&D and marketing headcount costs (down $9.8M and $6.2M) from CSG-organization consolidation drove the gain, partly offset by $27.1M higher other operating expense from merger and restructuring costs.

Tracks the operating-income gain plus D&A add-back. Qorvo's release names EBITDA as a non-GAAP measure methodologically but doesn't publish a dollar figure for it this quarter, so this KPI is Yahoo-timeseries-derived and not company-cross-checked.
Follows the operating-profit surge; income tax expense rose to $14.7M from $6.1M in dollar terms despite the effective rate falling to 14.6% from 19.2%, only partly offsetting the pretax-income gain.

Grew faster than net income because weighted diluted shares fell 4.7% y/y to 89.4 million from 93.8 million, even though no stock was repurchased this quarter; the decline reflects prior periods' buybacks rolling off the average.
Same share-count effect as diluted EPS — basic weighted shares fell 5.2% y/y to 88.0 million from 92.9 million on prior periods' buybacks.

Revenue fell 4.2% y/y on the ACG mix-shift away from mass-market Android, but margin expansion and lower opex drove operating income to $96.8M and diluted EPS to $0.96 from $0.27; management now expects FY2027 non-GAAP EPS above $7.00.
